Check locally

From the package root:

source("tools/check_package.R")

This installs development dependencies if needed and calls rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = "--no-manual", error_on = "warning"). The check runs examples and the test suite. LaTeX is not required. No CRAN submission is attempted.

For a faster development cycle, with devtools installed:

devtools::load_all()
devtools::test()
devtools::check(args = "--no-manual")

Or, after installing the package, check its examples from any folder:

source(system.file("examples", "quickstart.R", package = "niceSMD"))

The Word test inspects the generated Open XML package for editable table cells and repeating headers. A structural check cannot establish visual page layout; also open the example documents in Word or LibreOffice.

Documentation maintenance

Help files in man/ are maintained directly. The short roxygen-style comments in R/ are explanatory; there is no roxygen generation step. Do not run devtools::document() expecting it to preserve these complete help pages. Update both a function’s signature and its .Rd usage when changing arguments.

Numerical tests

The tests compare ordinary continuous and binary SMDs with explicit formulas, multilevel categorical SMDs with a covariance-matrix calculation, weighted continuous SMDs with survey variances, and weighted categorical SMDs with weighted proportions. They also cover weight scaling, missing-value denominators, character variables, numeric categorical overrides, duplicate labels, punctuation in names, zero weights, missing groups, constants, insufficient observations, and complex survey/replicate designs.

SMD calculation failures are recorded in the result rather than silently losing values. Inspect tab$smd$status and tab$smd$reason in your analysis.

Local source install without helper scripts

From a terminal in the package root:

R CMD build .
R CMD INSTALL niceSMD_0.1.0.tar.gz
R CMD check --no-manual niceSMD_0.1.0.tar.gz

Install Imports and Suggests dependencies first. The helper scripts do that for you. No user data is included in the package; examples are synthetic.
